subject: Why ordering of plots in facet_wrap is alphabetical?

messages.author: a1331fc093f52833
messages.subject: Why ordering of plots in facet_wrap is alphabetical?
parts:
Dear ggplot2 users,

It took me a while to find out that the ordering of the graphs in
facet_wrap is automatically alphabetical. See the following facet_wrap
example:

######################
n <- 100; x1 <- cbind(1:n,rnorm(n,sd=10)); x2 <-
cbind(1:n,rnorm(n,sd=3))
df <- data.frame(rbind(x1,x2)); names(df) <- c("x","y"); df$metric <-
as.factor(c(rep("A",n),rep("B",n)));
bi <- ggplot(df, aes(x=x)) + geom_line(aes(y=y)) +
facet_wrap(~metric,nrow=1,ncol=2); print(bi)
######################

If one changes the factors' levels, you obtain a different ordering,
such as:

######################
n <- 100; x1 <- cbind(1:n,rnorm(n,sd=10)); x2 <-
cbind(1:n,rnorm(n,sd=3))
df <- data.frame(rbind(x1,x2)); names(df) <- c("x","y"); df$metric <-
as.factor(c(rep("B",n),rep("A",n)));
bi <- ggplot(df, aes(x=x)) + geom_line(aes(y=y)) +
facet_wrap(~metric,nrow=1,ncol=2); print(bi)
######################

I perfectly understand the logic behind ordering the graph in an
alphabetical order, but is there a way for the user to control whether
this is the case?

Best wishes,
Cedric

messages.subject: Re: Why ordering of plots in facet_wrap is alphabetical?
parts: You can achieve order control like this ...

# Important Line Below
df$metric <- factor(df$metric,levels=c("B","A"))
# Important Line Above
